## Audience evidence and limits

There are three distinct audiences: Host, PC0 and PC1. The additional SourceCreature
channel aliases PC1's same full raw/presented view and revision; it is not a fourth
private audience. PC1 is uninvolved before assignment but is the actual reactor
controller during the OA; no claim of uninvolved OA privacy is made for it.

PC0's entire presented DTO, revision and handles remain equal across the private
source attack admission. PC1/source's entire presented DTO remains equal across
the holder's release. The canonical secret Grapple-save raw ID is absent from all
saved Player presentations. Player presentations omit Host diagnostics. Opaque
roll IDs join to each audience's retained projection handles and the same canonical
raw ID. PC0 sees no pending OA roll; PC1 and source alias share opaque
`46cfda92-b595-4245-ab91-0a039b7056c1`. The ordinary PC1 character channel is
correctly refused roll options (`Select the character who owns this roll.`), while
the real source channel receives valid options and submits the accepted answer.
Alias view equality therefore does not imply interchangeable command authority.

This is a valid frozen old-build baseline for a future independent consumer. It
does not prove the mass/new-version consumer can restore, reproduce DTO/retry bytes
or continue these cuts. The two Inspiration routes and strict Clippy remain pending
for the three-route capture allocation. Full canonical verification, CI, native
play and remaining Gate4 requirements are not inferred. Every Physical face here
is a controlled automated QA value; no human throw or native desktop evidence.
